Question_Text: Optimize Micro and Macro Space, analyzing performnce to determine space allocations for cateogires (macro) and  individual products (micro) to optimize sales densities (per square meter/foot), revenue and margin
Emerging: Manual data collection and spreadsheet data manipulation to prepare data for planogramming process. Typically performed at chain level .
Developing: Macro (Category) and Micro (product) space allocations planned in isolation, not considering cross category influences or Customer behaviors/shopping missions. Typically generated at chain level based on store formats and available space. Sales densities of categories and products not actively measured
Practicing: Space allocation consider product affinities to promote specific baskets and Customer behaviors. Typically generated at chain level based on store formats and available space. Sales densities of categories and products seen as a critical KPI for store sales performance comparisons
Innovating: Space allocations consider local customer behaviors and shopping missions. Typically stores are clustered by Customer behaviors /shopping missions
Leading: Dynamic space flexing to consider changes in shopping behaviors during the week and different shopping behaviors at weekend (e.g. smaller missions through the week, larger missions at weekend).
Roles: Business Sponsor
Industries: Retail; Financial; Communications; Manufacturing; Travel & Transport; Energy & Natural Resources; Healthcare
Review_Types: Big Data Capability Review; Data Warehouse Maturity Review; AI and Machine Learning Review; Custom Review

Question_Text: Optimize Assortments / Ranges or Product Mix, including building a product assortment / product mix by channel or location to reflect customer shopping behaviours
Emerging: Typically assortment proliferates as new products are introduced without removing existing products, driving low sales densities due to too many slow moving product. Ranging decisions based on product sales performance.
Developing: Centralised assortments based on store demographics formats and price bands. Ranging decisions based on product sales performance.
Practicing: Store cluster assortments optimized using product affinities, Ranging decisions based on basket analysis , to understand which products are important to which basket types.
Innovating: Assortment based on understanding of Customer behaviors and shopping missions in individual stores. Stores clustered based on like behaviors. Ranging decisions made with Customer behavior and shopping missions in mind. Product affinities from on-line transactions used to inform store ranging decisions
Leading: More localized assortments based on individual stores Customer behaviors and shopping missions (typically a core cluster range, with a proportion “localized” to individual stores. Product affinities from on-line transactions used to inform store ranging decisions. Able to incorporate local traffic and population data from prospective customer intelligence into range decisions.
Roles: Business Sponsor
Industries: Retail; Financial; Communications; Manufacturing; Travel & Transport; Energy & Natural Resources; Healthcare
Review_Types: Big Data Capability Review; Data Warehouse Maturity Review; AI and Machine Learning Review; Custom Review

Question_Text: Support Product Clearance, to dispose of excess or aged inventory to optimise sell through, markdowns and margins by modeling reduced prices and best locations in which to liquidate a product by an end date
Emerging: Excess inventory distributed to locations based on their size and sales, No consideration of their previous sales performance of the product or how much stock they already have
Developing: Excess inventory allocated to locations based on their size and their previous sales of the products – no consideration of existing stockholding
Practicing: Excess inventory allocated to locations based on their size, their previous sales of the products and existing stockholding
Innovating: Excess inventory distributed to locations based on each locations forecasted sales and current inventory, balanced to give each location the same inventory cover so clearance is synchronized across all locations
Leading: Leading organizations will have identified the potential issue of excess inventory before it occurs by using future inventory projections highlighting potential excess stock situations giving them the opportunity to circumvent the excess inventory – reduced orders, order delay, advertising etc.
Roles: Business Sponsor
Industries: Retail; Communications; Manufacturing; Travel & Transport; Energy & Natural Resources
Review_Types: Big Data Capability Review; Data Warehouse Maturity Review; AI and Machine Learning Review; Custom Review

Question_Text: Determine Product Migration is the identification and prioritization of products to be decommissioned and migrated to selected new products, optimizing customer value and business benefits
Emerging: Determine products for decommissioning based on number of customers owning the product or general sales volumes. Migrate to products based on current new product sales targets. Little or no understanding of customer and business impact
Developing: Determine products for decommissioning based on number of customers owning the product or general sales volumes, as well as some insight on product utilization. Migrate to products based on current new product sales targets and product attributes to meet customer utilization needs. Basic understanding of customer and business impact
Practicing: Basic application of analytical techniques to determine products for decommissioning as well as recommended new product, based on product utilization and product portfolio ownerships. Initial understanding of costs associated with the product.
Innovating: Application of analytical techniques to determine products for decommissioning as well as recommended new product, based on customer value , customer satisfaction and customer behavior. Significant understanding of costs and complexity associated with the product. Good understanding of customer and business impact.
Leading: Application of advanced analytical techniques to determine products for decommissioning as well as recommended new product, based on extensive customer insight and customer influential impact on customer base value.  Analytics also inform about timing of recommended migration. Full understanding of customer and business impact, including predicted indirect impact.
Roles: Business Sponsor
Industries: Retail; Financial; Communications; Manufacturing; Travel & Transport; Energy & Natural Resources; Healthcare
Review_Types: Big Data Capability Review; Data Warehouse Maturity Review; AI and Machine Learning Review; Custom Review

Question_Text: Optimize Reduce to Clear is the reduction of wastage and optimization of margin on perishable products that come to the end of their shelf life via intra-day analytics
Emerging: Manual checking of shelves to find products near end of shelf life. Manual consideration of  potential excess stock Undirected arbitrary local price reductions which dilute margin and sales revenue
Developing: Manual checking of shelves to find products near end of life. Central price reduction recommendations, typically a set percentage discount. no consideration of levels of excess stock
Practicing: Manual checking of shelves to find products near end of life, Set guidelines of discounts for locations for follow depending on excess stock
Innovating: Central calculation of potential excess stock levels in each location, alerts to stores. Dynamic pricing calculations to  optimize sell through, margin and wastage
Leading: Central calculation of potential excess stock levels in each location using hourly sales to pick up last minute opportunities, alerts to stores, Dynamic pricing calculations  and timing calculations using within day sales to  optimize sell through, margin and wastage
Roles: Business Sponsor
Industries: Retail
Review_Types: Big Data Capability Review; Data Warehouse Maturity Review; AI and Machine Learning Review; Custom Review

Question_Text: Support Product Recalls, to leverage customer purchase history to efficiently and proactively notify users of recalled products whilst optimizing costs and processes associated with them
Emerging: No proactive response to product recalls.  Customers may hear about the recall  from public news sources, not from the manufacturer or seller. Identifying and factoring in new information (e.g. Engineering and Manufacturing) to understand/diagnose drivers of recalls and to monitor and track outstanding ones.
Developing: POS data is mined to identify specific customers who purchased a recalled product.  Customers are proactively notified that a product that they purchased may have been affected by a product recall. Customer is responsible for checking model, lot or manufacturing dates to determine if their purchased product is affected. Recall notification takes weeks to process. Periodic use of new data types/streams (e.g. Engineering and Manufacturing) to better forecast recalls, understand/diagnose drivers of recalls and to monitor and track outstanding ones.
Practicing: Monitor social site mentions of product to identify optimal platform on which to issue information and further updates on recall. Incorporate social media data with historical sales and web data  to capture changes in brand or product sentiment.  Leverage personalization to respond to changes. Leveraging analytics on all relevant, integrated data sets to forecast recalls, manage them from end-to-end, and more surgically identify specific products to recall from the field.
Innovating: Manufacturers track lineage of products at all points in the production cycle.  Integrated traceability data helps to identify root cause and to respond quicker. Leverage detailed data to improve negotiations with suppliers to recoup recall costs.  Manufacturers can isolate defective components or defective lots, avoiding massive blanket recalls. Recalls are focused only on affected lots and the affected customers. Recall notifications take hours to process.
Leading: Quality Managers routinely scrape customer comments to identify issues, then  adjust quality parameters accordingly. Track variances  in historical patterns (such as returns) to foresee problems. Establish a temporary or permanent data exchange infrastructure to make affected customer data available  to manufacturers. Use of comprehensive and prescriptive analytical models that reduce recalls and associated costs  to industry –leading levels. Analytics used for management of recalls and to better inform product design and manufacturing processes.
Roles: Business Sponsor
Industries: Retail; Communications; Manufacturing; Energy & Natural Resources; Healthcare
Review_Types: Big Data Capability Review; Data Warehouse Maturity Review; AI and Machine Learning Review; Custom Review

Question_Text: Analyzing Market Basket and Affinity to leverage transaction level data to develop insight into customer behaviour, shopping missions and affinity
Emerging: Measure basic basket metrics such as basket size, revenue, and gross margin by location.  Incorporate affinity coefficients to understand driver and passenger items. Score and compare basket trips types by location across time. Identify key shopper missions by location.  Uncover regional variances and opportunities to improve assortments.   Compare location basket size and profitability to district or region to identify outliers.
Developing: Leverage affinity analytics to build bundles, promotions and select advertised items. Extend analytics to include real estate attributes such as location selling size, location format and type. Track impact of basket metrics when competitors move in or out of markets or before, during and after promotions. Requires promo data. Companies design and develop Executive Dashboard to track basket segments
Practicing: Compare composition of baskets across channels. Analyze baskets of items that have traits that are trending (ex: organic, imported, high brand recognition or hot trend), Evaluate driver items as candidates for private label development.  Leverage market research along with key traits of current driver items to influence design of items in the  product development pipeline.  Requires extended product trait data and product development data.
Innovating: Tailor format and layout of store to unique shopper segments of each location. Analyze customer segments (based  on trip mission) and the allocation of space to each trip segment by location. Identify mis-alignment of space and assortments. Requires planogram and assortment data
Leading: Analyze ecommerce baskets to understand motivations for buying, starting with what item was placed into the market basket first. Understand impact of promoting “basket starters”.  Adjust promotional strategies and tailor offers to customers during the visit accordingly.  Expand findings from ecommerce baskets to influence catalogue features, store layouts, end cap presentations, promotions and pricing.   Requires ecommerce transaction and cart detail.
Roles: Business Sponsor
Industries: Retail; Financial; Communications; Manufacturing; Travel & Transport; Energy & Natural Resources; Healthcare
Review_Types: Big Data Capability Review; Data Warehouse Maturity Review; AI and Machine Learning Review; Custom Review

Question_Text: Analyze cross-channel performance to support the identification of opportunities for product bundling, cross- or up-selling and product wraps
Emerging: Basic channels tracked. Channel data typically siloed with little or no integration of functional matrices. Inventory typically housed within different warehouses with no consistent tracking of product codes/ numbers. Little or no campaign tracking capability that allows for response tracking across products. Most channels owned by different business units are not coordinated. Little or no automation at any level
Developing: Channel management is entirely ad hoc, cross-channel delivery for acquisition activities not available. Organization is focused on driving costs out of the channel processes and maximizing individual sales.  Detailed transactional and financial information is typically not available immediately. Multi channel coordination typically sporadic or non-existent, Cross-channel cooperation improving but manual
Practicing: Multi-channel delivery and performance tracking. Organization defines and creates standard metrics for enterprise analysis.  Scorecards are built integrating results across business functions including limited non-financial data. Sporadic levels of automation. Little understanding of customer’s channel preference and limited resource optimization. Some integration of results across business functions. Gradual improvement in product ID’s to enable easy tracking of inventory across acquiring channels and originating warehouses
Innovating: Data analytics used to manage channel performance. Delivery and utilization is consistent with pre-defined metrics and business triggers.  Financial data is integrated with non-financial data to provide comprehensive reporting and analytic capabilities. Multi channel integration between web and static channels (in- and out-bound), sales force automation applications used with tracking capabilities. Extensive business rules used to manage channel delivery. KPI’s covering sales, customer satisfaction, inventory levels  and operational efficiency are embedded
Leading: Fully automated analytics used to track multiple products across multiple channels. Messages coordinated across all channels in a sequential, logical and consistent manner. Customer channel preferences are embedded in all product and service strategies. Extensive use of channel mix and capacity optimization techniques Contact strategy and acquisition activities adapted to customer preference based on logical channel rules. Common channel tracking enabling acquisition from one locality and returns through another  or seamless inventory fulfillment from multiple warehouses across different branch, brand or geographic location
Roles: Business Sponsor
Industries: Retail; Financial; Communications; Manufacturing; Travel & Transport; Energy & Natural Resources; Healthcare
Review_Types: Big Data Capability Review; Data Warehouse Maturity Review; AI and Machine Learning Review; Custom Review

Question_Text: Manage Open to Buy.  Manage forward financial plans at a product level, optimizing the sales potential by product class or sub-class and location whilst also reducing inventory excess through the timely purchase of new or replacement stock
Emerging: Open to buy calculation is managed at category or department level on a monthly basis.  May be manual or excel based worksheet.  Sales forecast are based loosely on trend data.
Developing: Leverage data-driven sales forecasting for more accurate open to buy estimates for some product lines.  Leverage sales contribution patterns to determine future sales and  inventory investments.
Practicing: Leverage algorithms to create accurate sales forecasts and inventory plans based on time-phased order forecasts for all products lines for each class or subclass by week or month.   What if scenario planning is used to explore potential sales and optimum required inventory for trending categories.  May manage open to buy projections for key items or key classifications. Incorporate detailed planning for units and currency with open to buy analytics. , Analytics are used to justify adjustments to current and future plans.
Innovating: Expand algorithms to create accurate sales forecasts and inventory plans based on time-phased order forecasts down to location level.  Very granular view of open to buy allowing imbalances of inventory across locations to be identified and addressed.  Algorithms/models are measured for accuracy and adjusted as needed.  Leverage “what if” modeling to explore scenarios based on potential sales, inventory orders, markdowns, budget etc.
Leading: Analytics are used to highlight trending products and potential gaps between planned and actual sales and inventory levels to identify opportunities to reallocate budget to maximize sales.  May incorporate alerts and operational dashboards to proactively respond to actual variances against planned open to buy.
Roles: Business Sponsor
Industries: Retail; Communications
Review_Types: Big Data Capability Review; Data Warehouse Maturity Review; AI and Machine Learning Review; Custom Review

Question_Text: Compare to Product Benchmarks by comparing a portfolio against an internal or external reference to identify gaps and potential enhancements
Emerging: Products and services are benchmarked against internal metrics with no formal mechanisms to identify feedback from the marketplace.
Developing: Ad-hoc collection of feedback from the marketplace to inform product design and change. Typically to solve known issues and dealing with daily or regular processes and tasks.
Practicing: Proactive and continuous feedback on significant KPIs across the product and channel range.
Innovating: Significant effort invested across the product lifecycle for tracking and managing KPIs with feedback actively considered and acted upon.
Leading: Primary mission of the business to achieve operational excellence with benchmarking taking a strategic role in driving business innovation. Numerous mechanisms to generate active feedback to improve products and services.
Roles: Business Sponsor
Review_Types: Big Data Capability Review; Data Warehouse Maturity Review; AI and Machine Learning Review; Custom Review

Question_Text: Manage Product Profitability, quantifying all product and services (P&S) revenue, cost and risks to calculate the true profitability over time
Emerging: Basic NPV profitability models built in Excel using summarized data calculated on an ad-hoc basis.
Developing: Basic Excel-based NPV models for key products/segments using summarised results from current/historic profit model.
Practicing: Basic product-level NPV model for existing product holdings only.
Innovating: Automated propensity models for some key products used to enhance product strategy with attrition models for existing product holdings, and propensity to buy models for new products.
Leading:
Full and automated future / lifetime value model for individual products which includes comprehensive coverage of:
Projected cash flows from existing product holdings.
Attrition models for existing product holdings.
Propensity to buy models for new products.
Behavioral usage models for non-contractual products.
Roles: Business Sponsor
Industries: Retail; Financial; Communications; Manufacturing; Travel & Transport; Energy & Natural Resources; Healthcare
Review_Types: Big Data Capability Review; Data Warehouse Maturity Review; AI and Machine Learning Review; Custom Review

Question_Text: Produce Behavioural Segmentations.  Determine and leverage insights or patterns derived from detailed data of customer's products and services usage to design and evolve products and promote pricing, range and promotions.
Emerging: Measure product consumption and usage of individual products pushed into the market to determine simple purchase and usage low-dimensional segments using some market research to understand customer needs but not infer them from data.
Developing: Mainly use of market and consumer survey techniques, and competitive information to design and evolve individual P&S with no deep consideration of broader consumer/customer behaviors and groups. Customise P&S according to simple consumption/usage segments and measure performance in those segments.
Practicing:
Design some specific P&Ss and promotions for specific usage/consumption segments and customer/consumer segments.
Use of market and consumer survey techniques, competitive information and internal usage/consumption patterns and segments to design and evolve individual P&S. Measure performance on those segments.
Innovating: Base existing product strategy and operation on customer centric analytics and segmentations that feed back into product design and lifecycle. Design P&Ss and promotions for specific usage/consumption segments and customer/consumer segments. Routinely go through existing data to detect new P&S opportunities.
Leading: Predict and influence customer consumption and usage behaviors based on high-dimensional customer behavioral segments and prediction of emerging segments to drive product strategy, design, evolution and lifecycle. Base existing product strategy and operation on customer centric analytics and segmentations that feed back into product design and lifecycle. Measure performance on existing customer segments
Roles: Business Sponsor
Industries: Retail; Financial; Communications; Manufacturing; Travel & Transport; Energy & Natural Resources; Healthcare
Review_Types: Big Data Capability Review; Data Warehouse Maturity Review; AI and Machine Learning Review; Custom Review

Question_Text: Predict Product/Service Retention, using analytics to predict products that are likely to support continued use by customers or to be dropped by customers
Emerging: Basic events and measures calculated for use in ad-hoc product retention activity.
Developing: Identification of different product retention/churn scenarios and key data correlating to produce retention models. Analytics used to drive the development of treatment strategies to address retention issues. Small number of retention campaigns run on monthly batch cycle.
Practicing: Retention model calculates customer segmentation based on product utilization which is used for weekly proactive retention campaigns. Single company understanding of product churn level definitions. Product affinity feeds into retention model.
Innovating: Product or service revenue retention campaigns executed on a daily basis using lifecycle knowledge including decline in usage, decline in product holding or reduced activity. Social network analysis (SNA) feeds influential relationships into retention model.
Leading: Streamline results into company strategy and processes automatically or make decisions to change business process based on insights. Cross channel Next Best Action (NBA) based on complex churn-value analytics running automatically driven by context and real-time triggers.
Roles: Business Sponsor
Industries: Retail; Financial; Communications; Manufacturing; Travel & Transport; Energy & Natural Resources; Healthcare
Review_Types: Big Data Capability Review; Data Warehouse Maturity Review; AI and Machine Learning Review; Custom Review

Question_Text: Support Contract Management, to monitor performance in-season against contract terms
Emerging: Little or no follow up to track collection of vendor monies associated with contract terms.  Focused on using commercial terms to reduce cost of goods without consideration of supply chain costs
Developing: Development of ad hoc reports to track actual performance vs. contract terms.   Manual integration of contract terms required. Little comparative analysis  across vendors or across departments.  Beginning to formalize a process of collating sales and cost data to support vendor negotiations.
Practicing: Vendor commercials consider impacts of supply chain costs and efficiencies. Quarterly review of key vendor performance statistics includes a review of negotiated terms and actual performance. Integrated sales, costs and inventory data available, but manual integration of contract terms is required for analysis
Innovating: Automated and timely reporting of contract term violations and their impacts. Timely and on demand vendor and product  performance analysis  is reviewed with vendors on a regular basis. Contract terms are tracked  and audited. Automated notification when contract terms or hurdle rates  are exceed
Leading: Centralized and standardized storage of contracts and extraction of terms from contracts for reporting purposes.  Exception analysis of commercial terms compliance and impacts identifying opportunities to improve future commercial terms and supply chain efficiencies.
Roles: Business Sponsor
Industries: Retail; Financial; Communications; Manufacturing; Travel & Transport; Energy & Natural Resources; Healthcare
Review_Types: Big Data Capability Review; Data Warehouse Maturity Review; AI and Machine Learning Review; Custom Review

Question_Text: Billing and Collections analysis to accelerate collections and reduce Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) and improve cash flow
Emerging: Billing and Collections processes are complex, subject to manual intervention, and disparate manual data collection, reconciliation, reporting and analysis.
Developing: Billing and Collections processes are partly automated, but still based on disparate data sourcing. Basic AR reporting (e.g. top 10%) is available.
Practicing: Billing and Collection processes are automated, and based on data sourced from an integrated data repository. Billing terms and conditions are automatically applied. Detailed historic AR reporting is available, and basic AR scorecard has been developed.
Innovating: Billing processes are automated using granular and timely data. Billing terms and conditions are automatically applied. Detailed information available in real-time to describe historic and current payment status . Future payment terms are set based on analysis of historic behaviour. Collection workflow based on simple rules.
Leading: Billing processes are automated using granular and timely data. Billing terms and conditions are automatically applied. Detailed information available in real-time to describe historic and current payment status. Future payment terms are set based on analysis of historic behaviour and/or 3rd party payment data. Automated collections decisioning, communications and actions based on predictive collections models & rules.
Roles: Business Sponsor
Industries: Retail; Financial; Communications; Manufacturing; Travel & Transport; Energy & Natural Resources; Healthcare
Review_Types: Big Data Capability Review; Data Warehouse Maturity Review; AI and Machine Learning Review; Custom Review

Question_Text: Procurement and Payment analysis to review purchase order compliance, manage goos receipts and manage suppliers to contract terms
Emerging: No link between Purchase Orders and Invoices. Analyses are done based on aggregated data extracts for limited periods and prepared in Excel files. Analyses are manual and time consuming and only done periodically.
Developing: Country ERP solutions have integrated Purchasing and Accounts Payable modules – but it is only possible to analyse Suppliers performance at an aggregated level. Analysis is manually intensive.
Practicing: Purchasing and AP data is linked in an ERP solution – but do not have the ability to work with data at the most granular data. Analyses are done on a regular basis, but still requires a lot of manual effort to prepare. Global view of Supplier performance and conditions are still limited as common definitions are not consistently used.
Innovating: Purchasing and AP data is linked either in an ERP solution or data warehouse. Detailed analyses of Supplier performance and Supplier conditions are done on a regular basis – typically following the Closing, Budget & Planning and/or the season for renegotiations (with Suppliers)
Leading: The Group has an integrated data warehouse, where all purchasing data and accounts payable data are available and updated real-time or daily. Pre-defined and ad hoc analyses can be done whenever needed. Everything is based on common definitions.
Roles: Business Sponsor
Industries: Retail; Financial; Communications; Manufacturing; Travel & Transport; Energy & Natural Resources; Healthcare
Review_Types: Big Data Capability Review; Data Warehouse Maturity Review; AI and Machine Learning Review; Custom Review

Question_Text: Sub-ledger accounting analyis to create centralised accounting processes and practises that are easier and cheaper to maintain and change whilst remaining compliant with all regulations.  Reducing reconciliation time between ledgers.
Emerging: Financial Accounting Processes  are either manually created or hard-coded into individual operational systems. Summary-level accounting data only passed to GL. No detailed accounting data is passed to the Data Warehouse.
Developing: Financial Accounting processes are hard-coded into individual operational systems. Summary level data is passed to GL, but some account-level accounting data is available (e.g. interest accruals) to feed the Data Warehouse.
Practicing: Financial Accounting processes are hard-coded into individual operational systems. Summary level data is passed to GL. The majority of account-level accounting data is available in the Data Warehouse and the reconciliation between the GL and Data Warehouse is significantly automated.  Manual Adjustments are only captured in the GL.
Innovating: An Accounting Hub solution is used for selected operational systems covering less complex requirements. Detailed accounting sub-ledger data is  generated and  integrated into the Data Warehouse for those operational systems, and the aggregated postings are passed to the GL.  Manual adjustments for these systems are originated in the sub-ledger and aggregated to the GL.
Leading: The Accounting Hub covers all operational systems and lines of business. Detailed accounting sub-ledger data is  generated and  integrated into the Data Warehouse  for those operational systems. All manual adjustments are originated in the sub-ledger and workflow approved.  Aggregated postings are passed to the GL.
Roles: Business Sponsor
Industries: Retail; Financial; Communications; Manufacturing; Travel & Transport; Energy & Natural Resources; Healthcare
Review_Types: Big Data Capability Review; Data Warehouse Maturity Review; AI and Machine Learning Review; Custom Review

Question_Text: Fair Value and Hedge Accounting, to mitigate the impact of adverse movements in volatile assets and commodities (eg. Currency, interest rates, fuel etc.)
Emerging: Fair Value & Hedge Accounting processes are manually-intensive and utilise disparate sources of data which are subject to validation and integration effort.
Developing: Fair Value & Hedge Accounting is performed using a dedicated application which sources data directly from disparate sources.
Practicing: Fair Value & Hedge Accounting is performed using a dedicated application, which sources data from a single integrated source.
Innovating: Fair Value & Hedge Accounting is performed on a somewhat automated basis using a dedicated application, which sources  all of the required data from a single integrated source.
Leading: Fair Value and Hedge Accounting is delivered as part of an integrated Accounting Hub solution. Rules-based calculation and accounting functionality enables Fair Value and Hedge Accounting to be performed on a largely automated basis, including detailed audit trail.  Analytical toolset supports hedge optimisation analytics.
Roles: Business Sponsor
Industries: Retail; Financial; Communications; Manufacturing; Travel & Transport; Energy & Natural Resources; Healthcare
Review_Types: Big Data Capability Review; Data Warehouse Maturity Review; AI and Machine Learning Review; Custom Review

Question_Text: Asset Valuations, to comply with relevant accounting and tax standards for valuation and identify impairments on a timely basis
Emerging: Asset valuations are calculated on a aggregate basis using manually-intensive processes. Data is obtained from disparate sources and is subject to manual  validation and integration effort.
Developing: Asset valuations are calculated on a mix of aggregate and granular basis. Some integrated data is used, however much is still obtained from disparate sources. Manual effort to source, validate and integrate data is still significant.
Practicing: Asset valuations are mostly calculated on a granular basis, and mostly use data from an integrated source. Manual effort to source, validate and integrate data is much reduced. Accounting calculations and rules are mostly hard-coded.
Innovating: Asset valuations are based on statistical and analytical models and meets all relevant accounting standards. Data used is mostly available from an integrated source. The process, including identification of impairments and creation of accounting entries, is mostly automated, but often hard-coded. Any manual intervention is managed using workflow functionality.
Leading: Asset valuations are based on sophisticated statistical and analytical models and meets all relevant accounting standards. Granular, integrated and up-to-date data is available with minimal manual effort, and a rules-based Accounting Hub is used to perform calculations, apply Accounting rules, and create accounting entries. Any manual intervention is managed using workflow functionality.
Roles: Business Sponsor
Industries: Retail; Financial; Communications; Manufacturing; Travel & Transport; Energy & Natural Resources; Healthcare
Review_Types: Big Data Capability Review; Data Warehouse Maturity Review; AI and Machine Learning Review; Custom Review

Question_Text: Reserve Analytics, to accurately estimate and account for future losses and/or establish reserves in recognition of anticipated debts, impairments, warranties, loyalty program costs etc.
Emerging: Reserves are set based on average historic loss  or redemption rates. Data is manually sourced and integrated using desktop tools (e.g. Excel / Access).
Developing: Introduction of basic statistical models to set reserves. Data is still obtained and integrated manually from multiple sources.
Practicing:
Reserves are calculated using basic statistical models based on granular historic data.
Automation of processes leveraging integrated data.
Innovating:
Reserves are calculated using more advanced statistical models based on granular historic data. 
Introduction of statistical techniques to more accurate calculate reserves balances using granular data
Leading: Reserves use advanced statistically-derived and/or advanced analytical models based on granular historic and unstructured data, sourced from an integrated data repository. Models are executed on an automated basis, proven to be historically accurate, and resulting accounting and reporting is delivered on a timely basis.
Roles: Business Sponsor
Industries: Retail; Financial; Communications; Manufacturing; Travel & Transport; Energy & Natural Resources; Healthcare
Review_Types: Big Data Capability Review; Data Warehouse Maturity Review; AI and Machine Learning Review; Custom Review

Question_Text: Tax Management and Optimisation, to efficiently and automatically calculate tax values and produce appropriate tax reporting
Emerging: Tax Management is performed manually (e.g. Excel / Access) using feeds of data from disparate General Ledger / ERP and other operational systems. Substantial manual effort is required.
Developing: Tax Management is still performed using desktop-based applications (e.g. Excel, Access) however some automation of data sourcing from disparate General Ledger / ERP and other operational systems has been introduced.
Practicing: Tax Management is performed using a dedicated solution which sources data directly from disparate General Ledger / ERP and other operational systems.
Innovating: Tax management is undertaken using a largely automated dedicated solution, which sources the majority of the required data from a single integrated and validated source. Tax optimisation and planning is delivered using this same source of data.
Leading: An Accounting Hub approach is used to deliver granular financial accounting, including tax calculations, and also tax aggregation and posting to the GL. Rules-based functionality enables tax rules to be maintained and updated easily. Tax return data can be produced on a largely automated basis with full drill-down and audit trail is available.
Roles: Business Sponsor
Industries: Retail; Financial; Communications; Manufacturing; Travel & Transport; Energy & Natural Resources; Healthcare
Review_Types: Big Data Capability Review; Data Warehouse Maturity Review; AI and Machine Learning Review; Custom Review

Question_Text: Reconciliation, Validation and Adjustment Analysis, to automate reconciliations, validations and adjustment processes as far as possible, and support audit trails of data to give confidence to accounting data users
Emerging: Reconciliation, Validation and Adjustment processes are fragmented and distributed widely across the organisation. They are largely manual, and involve extensive use of reports and spreadsheets.
Developing: Reconciliation and Validation are subject to some centralisation, with some use of common tools and processes.  However the underlying data upon which they operate is still fragmented, and needs to be sourced directly. Adjustments  are applied manually.
Practicing: A dedicated tool or solution is used to perform Reconciliation & Validation on a largely automated basis against data which is largely available from a single source. Adjustments are still primarily applied manually.
Innovating: Reconciliation, Validation and Adjustments are centralised, with well-defined and documented responsibilities and processes. A dedicated tool or solution is used to perform these processes on a largely automated basis against data which is largely available from a single source.
Leading: Reconciliation, Validation and Adjustments are centralised and automated, with well-defined and documented responsibilities. A best-in-class tool or solution is used, with exceptions requiring action being delivered via workflow functionality. Adjustments are integrated into both financial systems and data warehouse/analytical systems.
Roles: Business Sponsor
Industries: Retail; Financial; Communications; Manufacturing; Travel & Transport; Energy & Natural Resources; Healthcare
Review_Types: Big Data Capability Review; Data Warehouse Maturity Review; AI and Machine Learning Review; Custom Review

Question_Text: Financial Consolidation, to provide timely, accurate and efficient reporting of consolidated financial information across multiple ERPs and legal entities
Emerging: Financial Consolidation is performed using desktop-based applications (e.g. Excel, Access), and relies on substantial manual effort to source, collate, map and integrate financial data. The financial close process is slow and top-line adjustments are only visible in the consolidated records.
Developing: Financial Consolidation is still performed using desktop-based applications (e.g. Excel, Access) however some automation of data sourcing from disparate General Ledger / ERP and other operational systems has been introduced. The financial close process is still time-consuming.

AML analysis is separate and within isolated functional unit from Fraud and Credit Risk functions.  Although much of the same data is used for these functional applications, data is not shared, i.e. resulting in unproductive data movement , replication, risk, and cost.
Developing: Realization that AML, fraud, Credit Risk analysis utilized a lot of the same data and detection schemes and data should be shared. Detection and monitoring of money flows across and within retail, commercial and corporate accounts and customer base.  Incorporate all products as potential vehicle for laundering money, e.g. mortgage early payoff, small business loan payoff, etc. Suspicious activity feeds Next Best Interaction protocol to ensure appropriate customer messaging
Practicing: Meld Foreign Account Tax Compliance Act (FATCA) compliance into AML data set, given it is a lot of the same data. Same data foundation is shared (funding model opportunity)  between AML, fraud, and Credit Risk functional units.  In addition, Customer Experience (marketing) also utilizes same data set to manage relationship.
Innovating: Incorporation of Path and Graph analysis functions to detect emerging paths to money laundering and suspicious  associations.
Leading: Operationalized advanced analytic functions  to troll for emerging anomalies suggestive of potential money laundering (e.g. Path and Graph functions).  Text analysis applied on communications between institutional agents (associates) and customer to detect suspicious dialogue.
Roles: Business Sponsor
Industries: Financial
Review_Types: Big Data Capability Review; Data Warehouse Maturity Review; AI and Machine Learning Review; Custom Review

Question_Text: Care Co-ordination - co-ordinate care for chronically ill patients/members to avoid adverse health events
Emerging: Data on members or patients is kept in separate data marts or applications.   Complex data is paper based or scanned in documents. The effort to coordinate care is primariy manual.
Developing: Integration of data to a 360 view of a patient that includes all medical treatments, tests, drugs, etc.  Also includes results of enagement with individuals.  Scheduling for services outside of traditional treatments is kept separate. Reporting is basic BI type of reporting.
Practicing: 360 View of the patient includes all interactions with care coordinator and includes  non-traditional data sources, such a transportation,  home care,etc.   Analytics  includes BI reportings, Dashboards and some predictive analytics.  Quality metrics are performed by a 3rd party solution.
Innovating: 360 view of the patient now integrates results of gaps in care  and dates when service was rendered to close the gap in care.  Predictives scores are included in the patient profile so care coordinators have more information about a patient, such as likely to use the ER due to distance from primary care doctor.  Providers have easy to access information about the patient care that highlights next best action for the patient.
Leading: Care teams have decision support automating outreach to patients based on predictive analytics ; reminders, coaching or indication of another adverse event to be avoided.  Outreach to patients is personalized and delivered via the channel of preference using HIPAA approved privacy and security.
Roles: Business Sponsor
Industries: Healthcare
Review_Types: Big Data Capability Review; Data Warehouse Maturity Review; AI and Machine Learning Review; Custom Review

Question_Text: Provider Management - manage contracts and performance of providers contracted with the healthcare organisation
Emerging: Data on providers is primarily from credientially data sources.  Contract metrics are stored in a spreasheet,  Reimbursement is based on an off the shelve fee schedule .  Reports are generated listing PMPM costs by provider.
Developing: Fee schedules  and capitation rates are stored in a claim adudication system and assigned to a product network.  Providers (practioners and physicians) are contractually tied to each network.  Reimbursement is defined by capitated PMPM monthly payment or fee schedules.  Quality reports are basically peer comparsion and measuring costs by treatment types PMPM.
Practicing: Reimbursements to providers is still based on fee for service/capitation.   Quality metrics are applied to the primary care physicians based on preventative care and other agreed upon metrics.  Annual bonsues are calculated based on a pre-defined set of metrics.  Good quality providers get special mention in provider directories.  Data for metric calculations is still outside of the data warehouse as is the provider quality metric contract agreements.
Innovating: Patients are attributed providers enrollment in value care based contracts.  Attribution models are based on selecting a primary care doctor or business rules involving office visits.  Value Based Payments are calculated on a quarterly basis evaluating utilization of patients attributed to care and a pre-defined set of quality metrics.  Analytics are still BI based and may be self-service.  Contract metrics are still kept silo’d by provider management department
Leading: Providers have access to information on patients who have been attributed to their care, which gaps are relavent, what other providers  the patients has obtained care and what the finanical thresholds are for the provider at this point in time based on agreed upon thresholds.  They have the ability to enter corrections based on medical chart information and attest to the validing of the data. Operations produces metrics tying claim adjustments, claim rejections and greivance calls to providers for administrative quality.  Identifcation of provider recruitment is based on quality metrics both medical and administrative.
Roles: Business Sponsor
Industries: Healthcare
Review_Types: Big Data Capability Review; Data Warehouse Maturity Review; AI and Machine Learning Review; Custom Review

Question_Text: Claims Management - Optimize claims processing of insurance and healthcare claims
Emerging: Claims processing is performed by a 3rd party.  All claims available for the data warehouse are adjudicated claims only.  KPIs, etc are produced by 3rd party.
Developing: Claims processing increases first pass resolution rate due to electronic submission of claims, benefits and authorizations maintained in a single system.  Claims that are loaded into a data warehouse are primarily adjudication claims.  Reports are standard operational KPIs with dashboards.
Practicing: Claims processing either in-house or by 3rd party has high rate of first pass resolution (no suspends) and low rate of errors (adjustments).  KPIs are dashboards and can tie productivity down to claim source and claim processor.  Claims that are captured for fraudulent analysis are adjudicated but may be captured prior to payments being sent out of house.  Claims submitted to a data warehouse is more frequent; such as daily.
Innovating: Claims submitted for adjudication but not yet paid can be loaded to a data warehouse to be an early identifier of a change in patient status.  Additional operational analytics is applied to daily loads of both adjudicated and suspended claims into a data warehouse to identify areas for processing improvement and support other time senstive analysis in the organization.  Analytics involves mining techniques.
Leading: Analyze in-coming EDI transactions to determine quality of coding for root cause remediation and possible fraudulent activity.  Compare in-coming EDI transactions to adjudicated claims and out-going EDI transactions for processing accuracy, compliancy of authorizations and claim outcome.  Target problem areas to reduce adminstriative cost and prevent complaints.   EDI transactions to be stored in HADOOP for big data type of data mining.
Roles: Business Sponsor
Industries: Financial; Healthcare
Review_Types: Big Data Capability Review; Data Warehouse Maturity Review; AI and Machine Learning Review; Custom Review

Question_Text: Pharmacy Management - Provide operational oversight and measurements in operations
Emerging: Billing and Collections processes automated, but disparate, Product is primary business focus, with little patient-centricity.  JIT logistics regularly exceed 10% write-offs due to diversion/ OOS/overstock/unsaleables.
Developing: Dispensing records and inventory management are separate; reports are in place for each and reconciliations regularly occur. Billing and Collections processes are primarily automated, but separate from actual practice. Basic AR/AP reporting in place, but no connection with actual Payor and Vendor interactions. JIT logistics are basic, with 5-10% write-offs due to diversion/ OOS/overstock/unsaleables.
Practicing: Drug utilization review is real-time, accurate information for product(s).  Drug information data is sourced from an interoperable data repository. Billing terms and conditions are automatically applied. Audit preparation is manual, accreditation is frequent.  Pharmacist time often split between dispensing/clinical. JIT logistics have room for improvement, with 2-5% write-offs due to diversion/OOS/overstock/unsaleables.
Innovating: Clinical care is common.  Medication reconciliation is ongoing.  Inventory and Dispensing are interoperable, with lean just-in-time stock.  Robotics, pumps, dispensing processes are automated using granular and timely data. Billing terms and conditions are automatically applied. Audit preparation is mostly electronic, accreditation common. DUR is automated and alerts are case-specific; alert fatigue is minimal.  Acute-care, chronic care transitions are regular and consistent. JIT logistics have 2% write-offs due to diversion/ OOS/overstock/unsaleables. clinical time is a significant factor, with PQA standards utilized.
Leading: Care teams are well coordinated, with EHR communications interoperable with analytics to assist practitioners with clinical results.  Computerized clinical decision-making is incorporated into practices and driven by Evidence-based medicine. Cost–effectiveness studies consistently achieve top results.  Audit preparation is streamlined, accreditation consistently maximized. JIT logistics regularly achieve below 2% write-offs due to diversion/OOS/overstock/unsaleables
Roles: Business Sponsor
Industries: Healthcare
Review_Types: Big Data Capability Review; Data Warehouse Maturity Review; AI and Machine Learning Review; Custom Review

Practicing:
Forecast performance measured at multiple levels, across multiple lags to support performance measures vs. various decision points (e.g. vendor contract time, production commit time, distribution time, etc…).  Evaluating the performance  (of forecasting) of advertising and promotional activities.
Multiple measures applied, consistent method of calculation across the organization.

Use of different historical data types – invoice, shipment, order, … to determine best method for supporting supply chain decisions.  Impact analysis of forecast error – tying to inventory value,, COGS, production variability, expediting costs.
Production/Supply delays highlighted to remove from “error” components caused by supply constraints.
Leading: Bringing in Economic and external information to identify causes of forecast error and incorporate into the forecast process to improve the actual forecast.  Example is weather data or new housing starts etc… that impact product usage in the long or short term.

Question_Text: Order Analysis - Optimising the accuracy of orders and the effective flow of inventory

Leads to “knee jerk” over-reactions  to either reduce inventory or reduce out of stocks in an on-going cycle. Many emergency orders raised out of the normal ordering cycle.

Practicing: Orders automatically reviewed against targets (eg stock cover generated, potential out of stocks)  generating exception alerts to highlight potential issues allowing majority of orders within target to be released automatically without manual review allowing users to focus on order exceptions and the underlying reasons  and tune ordering parameters where appropriate.
Innovating: Orders automatically reviewed against targets (eg stock cover generated, potential out of stocks)  generating exception alerts to highlight potential issues allowing majority of orders within target to be released automatically without manual review . System automatically identifies causes of exceptions and recommends adjustments
Leading: Automated process for monitoring ordering parameters to remain within targets, highlighting potential ordering issues before they arise, providing the use with “what if” capability to model the optimum replenishment parameters going forward. Need a long term demand and inventory plan  detailing projected orders and deliveries to support the process.

Question_Text: Product Lifecycle Management - actively manage products through their lifecycles to ensure the most appropriate stocking and inventory management policies are applied at each lifecycle stage

Tracking early product  performance by location by day, to identify potential under and over stock situation allowing early reaction to ensure stock is optimally balanced across all locations

Manual management of supply chain constraints through the lifecycle, typically reactive, not planned and proactive

Leading:
Agile hold and flow techniques employed to ensure the right inventory goes to the right stores based on early life performance, integrated with allocation and replenishment solutions
End of life residual stock position automatically predicted  in each location with recommendations of remedial actions to ensure optimal sell through to drive margin and revenue

Question_Text: Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP) - To evaluate and actively balance future demand and supply, to plan production, capacity, resources and inventory, linking to the business/financial plan

Developing: More formal “Excel” based reporting process, single owner, more consistency of data, but still issues over synchronisation of data  extracts and granularity of data resulting in inaccurate KPIs. S&OP review process formalised with regular (weekly/monthly) review cycles
Practicing: Formal S&OP tool with drill down capability, documentation of assumptions, systematic approach to data source and integration.  Ability to do root cause and view Aggregate to detailed level of S&OP hierarchy for all products/services. Exception capability to highlight potential issues.
Innovating:
Ability to do “what-if” analysis for supply constraints and to adjust plans and allocate product by profitability/key customers etc…
Financial components (e.g. reports in currency, not just quantity) being used to help drive decisions on demand/supply and profitability.
Leading: Brining in Economic and external information to identify/predict causes of demand and supply changes.  These are incorporated in the planning process to improve the plan as well as understand financial implications.  Example is weather data or new housing starts etc… that impact product usage in the long or short term.  Other examples include a hurricane that reduces product supply from a given region/port and will cause changes that impact inventory/supply/demand for a period of time.
Roles: Business Sponsor
Industries: Retail; Financial; Communications; Manufacturing; Travel & Transport; Energy & Natural Resources; Healthcare
Review_Types: Big Data Capability Review; Data Warehouse Maturity Review; AI and Machine Learning Review; Custom Review

Question_Text: Supply Network Optimisation - Optimise the Supply Chain Network by identifying the ideal locations for manufacturing facilities, warehouses, and /or distribution and fulfillment centers
Emerging: No automated approach to determining locations of facilities or transportation lanes/provider.  Decisions are based upon minimal analysis of historical data intended to predict future requirements. Decisions made in isolation with no consideration of impacts on other operations or the wider supply chain.
Developing: Infrequent use of basic high level  information to occasionally review current network structure and make minor changes to improve flow of good through the supply chain. Data isn’t integrated therefore most decisions are made in isolation and don’t consider  wider supply chain implications
Practicing: Regular use of consolidated data to foster an on-going review of the current network structure.  Includes use of future projected volumes by regions and/or demographics to provide the ability to plan and recommend future changes. Majority of time is still spent on collecting and consolidating data from multiple systems.
Innovating:
Creation of a single view of integrated , consistent supply chain data which drives regular  pre-emptive modification to transportation network design and/or providers as well as future projected requirements. Decisions consider the wider supply chain implications with the ability to model the impact of changes on the rest of the supply chain.
Use of on-line demand and delivery geo-spatial  data to plan on-line fulfilment modes and locations (eg service from DC, existing Store or fulfilment centre)
Leading: Real time analysis of predicted demand used to dynamically change transportation requirement and drive facility optimization to react to potential demand changes across the network.
Roles: Business Sponsor
Industries: Retail; Financial; Communications; Manufacturing; Travel & Transport; Energy & Natural Resources; Healthcare
Review_Types: Big Data Capability Review; Data Warehouse Maturity Review; AI and Machine Learning Review; Custom Review

Question_Text: Distribution / Fulfillment Performance Analysis - Provide the ability to measure, predict and enhance the performance of distirbution and fulfillment activities
Emerging: Manual system of data entry and collection of internal and external data required to report performance metrics on a weekly or monthly  frequency. Typically based around each location, no overall visibility of performance.
Developing: Some integration with 3PL providers and internal data sources such that daily or weekly reporting of performance metrics is accomplished for most all operations within the supply chain. Inconsistent reporting of performance data across different locations.
Practicing: Automated consolidation and integration of all data within the supply chain (both internal and external providers) enabling consistent daily reporting of all distribution, fulfilment and transportation functions to all operating personnel.
Innovating: Near real time ability to report performance in all areas of the logistics execution service areas, providing visibility of potential bottlenecks allowing pre-emptive actions to mitigate impacts.
Leading: Real time ability to know report and predict performance in all areas of the logistics execution service areas (distirbuiton center, fulfilment operation and transportation).  This includes the ability to provide advanced notification to customers and trading partners of future expected delivery ETA as well as regular updates as required.
Roles: Business Sponsor
Industries: Retail; Financial; Communications; Manufacturing; Travel & Transport; Energy & Natural Resources; Healthcare
Review_Types: Big Data Capability Review; Data Warehouse Maturity Review; AI and Machine Learning Review; Custom Review

Question_Text: Lot / Batch Track and Trace - Provide the ability to quickly identify the history associated with products and components/ingredients to minimise impact and financial exposure
Emerging: Manual system of data entry and collection of supplier and manufacturing data.  Location specific, no overall visibility of data. No capability to trace causes or impacts of issues.
Developing: Some integration with suppliers and other partners in the supply chain to track component products/ingredients as well as movement of goods throughout the supply chain. Still no overall visibility of data. Limited capability to trace causes or impacts of issues
Practicing: Regular automated consolidation and  integration of all key manufacturing data to allow for a full view of products components as well as storage locations and point of sale (POS). Enables causal analysis and impact analysis of issues, with focussed recall activities
Innovating: Integrated data with both suppliers as well a retailers which ties lot/batch activity to consumer purchases at the point of purchase. Full visibility of product history allowing granular causal and impact analysis with highly focussed recall activities (Capability includes the ability to initiate rapid communication with will parties effected by impacted product)
Leading:
Real time ability to know the location of all lots and batches of a product, allowing immediate remedial actions (eg stopping production line, distribution etc)  This capability includes both internal and external locations, including consumer contact information (phone, address, etc).  
Analysis of historical issues and impacts to predict and pre-empt future issues.
Roles: Business Sponsor
Industries: Retail; Financial; Communications; Manufacturing; Travel & Transport; Energy & Natural Resources; Healthcare
Review_Types: Big Data Capability Review; Data Warehouse Maturity Review; AI and Machine Learning Review; Custom Review

Question_Text: Shipment / Load Planning - Improve supply chain cost effectiveness and service levels by optimizing the shipment and load planning process
Emerging: Ad-hoc, no automated approach, manual collection and interpretation of data to support consolidation of container loads of single sku / single vendor truck loads
Developing: Time interval, No automated approach, manual collection and interpretation of data to support consolidation of multiple sku, single vendor truck loads
Practicing: Automated time interval,  rule based analysis of data to aggregate multiple sku per vendor using demand / order projections not only of next bulk order but also of future bulk orders for order pull forward
Innovating:
Active automated time interval, rule based container load suggestions based on multiple sku over multiple vendors  based on incoterms (eg. FOB consolidation per source mainport for far east container deliveries) for upcoming delivery using pull forward.
Modelling ordering, transport, distribution constraints to optimise container fill through demand shaping and joint replenishment processes
Leading:
Active automated time interval, rule based container load suggestions based on multiple sku over multiple vendors  based on incoterms (eg. FOB consolidation per source mainport for far east container deliveries).
Ability to perform “what  if” scenario analysis to determine the optimum way of executing the load
Roles: Business Sponsor
Industries: Retail; Communications; Manufacturing; Travel & Transport; Energy & Natural Resources
Review_Types: Big Data Capability Review; Data Warehouse Maturity Review; AI and Machine Learning Review; Custom Review

Question_Text: Availability / Lost Sales Analysis and Optimisation - Improve product availability through the prediction and active management fo potential lost sales situations
Emerging: Manual, infrequent silo’d, summarised, measurement of on shelf availability, typically, spreadsheet based, using end of day inventory levels to calculate availability. Availability typically based on number of products in range which are out of stock (no consideration of volume)
Developing: More systematic reporting of on shelf availability using BI tool. Considers sales volume of each out of stock item to provide a demand weighted view  of availability, still based on end of day inventory and only considers full days of out of stock – typically inaccurate for slow moving products
Practicing: Causal analysis of poor availability with basic calculations of lost sales by comparing actual sales to forecast sales. Ability to track causes of lost sales back through the supply chain to identify opportunities to improve systemic issues (forecast accuracy, supplier performance, lead times etc)
Innovating:
Employing different probability modelling techniques for slow and fast moving products 
Using with in day sales to identify when  a product went off sale (before end of day) and when it came back on sale (after start of day) and calculate an accurate lost sales based upon a demand model
Using probability models to identify  potential out  of stock situations of slow moving giving a more accurate assessment
Leading: Using near time sales to predict and identify  potential lost sales  of fast moving products and generate alerts to warn stores to check deliveries, back room stock to ensure product is available to sell.
Roles: Business Sponsor
Industries: Retail; Communications; Manufacturing; Travel & Transport; Energy & Natural Resources
Review_Types: Big Data Capability Review; Data Warehouse Maturity Review; AI and Machine Learning Review; Custom Review

Question_Text: Supply Chain Visibility - Provides the end to end, time phase inventory visibilty by product and inventory status throughout the enterprise
Emerging: Manual system of data entry and collection of internal and external data required to track inventory and associated costs throughout the supply chain. Typically by location with little integration or visibility across the supply chain
Developing: integration of high level summarised data with 3PL providers and internal data sources such that a daily or weekly snapshot of inventory, orders, shipments and costs throughout the supply chain is available to the organization.
Practicing: Regular automated consolidation and  integration of all detailed data within the supply chain (both internal and external providers) so that current and future inventory plans are available throughout the supply chain. Provides consistent data and reporting KPI’s across the supply chain
Innovating: Near real time ability to report inventory and costs in all areas of the supply chain, highlighting potential future inventory issues
Leading: Real time visibility to inventory  and costs throughout the supply chain supporting supply chain planning and risk mitigation activities.  This includes the ability to provide detailed costs at the SKU level and rolled up at facility and/or customer views.
Roles: Business Sponsor
Industries: Retail; Financial; Communications; Manufacturing; Travel & Transport; Energy & Natural Resources; Healthcare
Review_Types: Big Data Capability Review; Data Warehouse Maturity Review; AI and Machine Learning Review; Custom Review

Question_Text: Order to Cash - Link Sales and Finance organisations, integrating sales with customer payments, returns, rebates etc to help determine true customer profitability
Emerging: No automated approach, manual collection and reporting of data.  Long latency on reporting and collection activities.
Developing: ERP supported reporting of sales and receivables data.  Timely, but limited to ERP capabilities, manual effort for identifying mismatches between terms, payments, prices, etc…
Practicing: Consolidated Receivables  information  and reports, on demand, by product,  customer, region, organization etc…  Alerts or rankings by payments not matching deliverables, currency conversion differences and other miss-matches between terms, conditions, expected and actual receivables.
Innovating: Balancing (optimizing) between terms, payments and price with customers to ensure on time payment, but considering all aspects of the total profitability of the goods.  Actions that support reduction of Days Sales Outstanding and cash collections.
Leading: Integrating ERP and ERP information at the most granular level to provide a definitive view of cash flow and accurate allocations of costs. Proactive monitoring of cash flow highlighting potential issues and challenges through exceptions  and alerts
Roles: Business Sponsor

Question_Text: Supply Chain Financial Performance Analysis - Drive better business decisions based on financial impacts and performance of the supply chain
Emerging: Manual, infrequent silo’d, summarised, measurement of basic supply chain performance , spreadsheet based. No consistency across locations.
Developing: Measure standard supply chain metrics (CPC, Labour rates, pick rates etc) using averages, weekly/monthly, semi-automated data capture and analysis. Still oriented to each location, no overall supply chain view.

Consistent reporting across the supply chain with exception analysis highlighting best/poor performing processes/locations.
Innovating:
Ability to capture, allocate and provide full visibility of all detailed cost through the supply chain to develop a detailed cost and profitability model by product, location and Customer at any point in time
Build profitability models over product lifetime. Build detailed cost to serve models to identify opportunities to drive efficiencies.

Question_Text: Quality Management - Provide an overall view across the entire value chain and life cycle to support consistent metrics, drive best pracitces and improve yield and customer satisfaction
Emerging: No automated approach, manual collection of data at summarised level. Segregated non-consistent approach
Developing: Semi automated KPIs calculation on transactional data or available ERP data. Collection and integration of data  usually in Excel or other limited access tools
Practicing: Integrated bottom up and top down view of company wide shared KPIs on manufacturing quality. Automated collection of data and display though dashboards and standardized reports
Innovating: Integrated bottom up and top down transparency  of quality KPIs expanded with discovery capabilities to search for and detect emerging quality issues
Leading: Real time KPI calculation based on data collected across the entire manufacturing process and life cycle.  External data (e.g. weather, AT) and other factors to relate to production quality/yield.  Sensor data analysis to determine quality of the actual sensors.

Question_Text: Manufacturing Performance - Improve the supply (production) capabilities of the manufacturing organisation in the most economical fashion

Developing: Siloes of reporting within and across sites.  Metrics are provided, but  little consistency in method and process.

Question_Text: Global Plant Visibility - Provide an overall view across all plants / facilities to support consistent metrics, drive best practices and improve yield

Question_Text: Fleet Management - Locate, manage and optimise fleet investments aligned with business strategy
Emerging: Manual system and processes for tracking fleet inventory and costs across some or all of the supply chain network.
Developing: Some integration within the organization to automate the location and utilization of the fleet.

Innovating: Near real time tracking of the location and utilization of the fleet.  The ability to track all operating costs down to the individual unit within the fleet.

Question_Text: Logistics Capacity Analysis - take long range plans and forecasts to create a roadmap required to ensure capacity for future growth exists

Innovating: Integrated supply chain data providing a single supply chain view. Regular modification to facility locations and sizes, processing areas to reflect future demand and capacity requirements,  transportation fleets and/or 3rd party providers. Exception reporting to predict and highlight potential capacity issues. “what –if” capability to determine impacts of changes to supply chain operations on the rest of the supply chain.
Leading: Real time analysis of predicted demand used to dynamically change logistics resources as required to maintain capacities at manageable levels and maintain supply chain service.

Question_Text: Logistics Efficiency Analysis -Analysis to ensure that the best logistics service is being provided at the most economical cost
Emerging: Manual, infrequent silo’d, summarised, measurement of basic Logistics performance, spreadsheet based. No consistency across facilities
Developing: Measure standard Logistics metrics (OTIF, pick rates, vehicle fill etc) weekly/monthly, semi-automated data capture and analysis by location/facility. No end to end visibility across the supply chain
Practicing:
Single integrated, consistent view of detailed supply chain performance data allowing comparisons of facilities performance 
On demand automated measurement of key logistics metrics and dashboards 
Assigning actual costs to detailed performance metrics to identify cost saving and efficiency opportunities
Timely evaluation of historical lane, mode , 3PL usage metrics
Innovating: Ability to capture, and provide full visibility of all Logistics performance metric and link to end Customer service achievement  identifying causes of service failures and identification of service improvement opportunities
Leading:
Real time visibility of logistics performance  used to make inflight changes  to manage risk from unplanned events and maintain service (eg flood in a DC redirect orders to other DC, expedite decision (fly v ship))

Prediction of future performance challenges based on analysis of historical performance allowing pre-emptive actions to alleviate or mitigate impacts and maintain service
Roles: Business Sponsor
